claim: BDNF controls the survival, growth, and function of neurons both during development and in the adult nervous system.
source: Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) controls the survival, growth, and function of neurons both during the development and in the adult nervous system.
evidence: This is a general statement about BDNF function that draws from established scientific consensus in the field.

claim: Bdnf is transcribed from several distinct promoters generating transcripts with alternative 5' exons.
source: Bdnf is transcribed from several distinct promoters generating transcripts with alternative 5' exons.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Bdnf gene structure.

claim: Bdnf transcripts initiated at the first cluster of exons have been associated with the regulation of body weight and various aspects of social behavior.
source: Bdnf transcripts initiated at the first cluster of exons have been associated with the regulation of body weight and various aspects of social behavior, but the mechanisms driving the expression of these transcripts have remained poorly understood.
evidence: This statement references prior research findings about the functional roles of specific Bdnf transcripts.

claim: An evolutionarily conserved intronic enhancer region inside the Bdnf gene regulates both basal and stimulus-dependent expression of Bdnf transcripts starting from the first cluster of 5' exons in mouse and rat neurons.
source: Here, we identify an evolutionarily conserved intronic enhancer region inside the Bdnf gene that regulates both basal and stimulus-dependent expression of the Bdnf transcripts starting from the first cluster of 5' exons in mouse and rat neurons.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by multiple experimental approaches including CRISPRi, CRISPRa, and deletion experiments shown in Figures 4, 5, and 7.

claim: A functional E-box element exists in the enhancer region, linking the expression of Bdnf and various pro-neural basic helix–loop–helix transcription factors.
source: We further uncover a functional E-box element in the enhancer region, linking the expression of Bdnf and various pro-neural basic helix–loop–helix transcription factors.
evidence: This finding is supported by luciferase reporter assays with E-box mutations shown in Figure 8G and 8H.

claim: During development, BDNF promotes the survival of various sensory neuron populations.
source: During the development, BDNF promotes the survival of various sensory neuron populations (Ernfors et al., 1994; Jones et al., 1994).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: In the adult organism, BDNF is required for the proper maturation of synaptic connections and regulation of synaptic plasticity.
source: In the adult organism, BDNF is also required for the proper maturation of synaptic connections and regulation of synaptic plasticity (Korte et al., 1995; Park and Poo, 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Defects in BDNF expression and signaling have been implicated in various neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative diseases, including major depression, schizophrenia, Alzheimer's disease, and Huntington's disease.
source: Defects in BDNF expression and signaling have been implicated in various neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative diseases, including major depression, schizophrenia, Alzheimer's disease, and Huntington's disease (Autry and Monteggia, 2012; Burbach et al., 2004; Jiang and Salton, 2013; Murray et al., 1994; Ray et al., 2014; Wong et al., 2010; Zuccato et al., 2001; Zuccato and Cattaneo, 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Rodent Bdnf gene contains eight independently regulated non-coding 5' exons (exons I–VIII) followed by a single protein-coding 3' exon (exon IX).
source: Rodent Bdnf gene contains eight independently regulated non-coding 5' exons (exons I–VIII) followed by a single protein-coding 3' exon (exon IX).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the structure of the rodent Bdnf gene.

claim: Splicing of one of the alternative exons I–VIII with the constitutive exon IX gives rise to different Bdnf transcripts.
source: Splicing of one of the alternative exons I–VIII with the constitutive exon IX gives rise to different Bdnf transcripts (Aid et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Transcription can start from an intronic position upstream of the coding exon producing an unspliced 5' extended variant of the coding exon (exon IXa-containing transcript).
source: Additionally, transcription can start from an intronic position upstream of the coding exon producing an unspliced 5' extended variant of the coding exon (exon IXa-containing transcript) (Aid et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Bdnf exon I-, II-, and III-containing transcripts show mainly nervous system-specific expression patterns.
source: For instance, Bdnf exon I-, II-, and III-containing transcripts show mainly nervous system-specific expression patterns, whereas Bdnf exon IV- and VI-containing transcripts are expressed in both neural and non-neural tissues (Aid et al., 2007; Timmusk et al., 1993).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Bdnf exon IV- and VI-containing transcripts are expressed in both neural and non-neural tissues.
source: For instance, Bdnf exon I-, II-, and III-containing transcripts show mainly nervous system-specific expression patterns, whereas Bdnf exon IV- and VI-containing transcripts are expressed in both neural and non-neural tissues (Aid et al., 2007; Timmusk et al., 1993).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Similar expression patterns for different BDNF transcripts are observed in humans.
source: Similar expression patterns for different BDNF transcripts are also observed in humans (Pruunsild et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Different Bdnf transcripts have distinct contribution to various aspects of neural circuit functions and behavior.
source: Notably, different Bdnf transcripts have distinct contribution to various aspects of neural circuit functions and behavior (Hallock et al., 2019; Hill et al., 2016; Maynard et al., 2016; Maynard et al., 2018; McAllan et al., 2018; Sakata et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Enhancers are usually active in a tissue- and cell-type-specific manner.
source: Enhancers are usually active in a tissue- and cell-type-specific manner (reviewed in Heinz et al., 2015; Wu et al., 2014), and can be located inside or outside, upstream or downstream of the target gene, within another gene or even on a different chromosome (Banerji et al., 1981; Lettice et al., 2003; reviewed in Ong and Corces, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research and reviews.

claim: Enhancers can be located inside or outside, upstream or downstream of the target gene, within another gene or even on a different chromosome.
source: Enhancers are usually active in a tissue- and cell-type-specific manner (reviewed in Heinz et al., 2015; Wu et al., 2014), and can be located inside or outside, upstream or downstream of the target gene, within another gene or even on a different chromosome (Banerji et al., 1981; Lettice et al., 2003; reviewed in Ong and Corces, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research and reviews.

claim: Many enhancers are activated only after specific stimuli, which cause enrichment of active enhancer-associated histone modifications and increased chromatin accessibility.
source: Many enhancers are activated only after specific stimuli, which cause enrichment of active enhancer-associated histone modifications and increased chromatin accessibility (Su et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Genome-wide analysis has proposed approximately 12,000 neuronal activity-regulated enhancers in cortical neurons.
source: Genome-wide analysis has proposed approximately 12,000 neuronal activity-regulated enhancers in cortical neurons (Kim et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Dysregulation of enhancers or mutations in proteins that participate in the formation of enhancer-promoter complexes is associated with a variety of disorders, including neurodegenerative diseases.
source: Importantly, dysregulation of enhancers or mutations in proteins that participate in the formation of enhancer-promoter complexes is associated with a variety of disorders, including neurodegenerative diseases (reviewed in Carullo and Day, 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a review.

claim: The induction of Bdnf mRNA after BDNF-TrkB signaling in neurons depends on unknown distal regulatory regions.
source: Notably, the induction of Bdnf mRNA after BDNF-TrkB signaling in neurons seems to depend on unknown distal regulatory regions (Esvald et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research from the authors' laboratory.

claim: Dopamine-induced expression of Bdnf in astrocytes is controlled by an unknown regulatory region within the Bdnf gene locus.
source: Furthermore, dopamine-induced expression of Bdnf in astrocytes is controlled by an unknown regulatory region within the Bdnf gene locus (Koppel et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research from the authors' laboratory.

claim: The +3 kb region is hypersensitive to DNaseI, indicative of an open chromatin structure.
source: First, the +3 kb region is hypersensitive to DNaseI, indicative of an open chromatin structure.
evidence: This is based on analysis of ENCODE ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The +3 kb region is enriched for H3K4me1, H3K4me3, and H3K27ac modifications.
source: Second, ChIP-seq data shows that this region is enriched for H3K4me1, H3K4me3, and H3K27ac modifications.
evidence: This is based on analysis of ENCODE ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The +3 kb region interacts with RNA polymerase II, with strong evidence for bidirectional transcription.
source: Third, the +3 kb region interacts with RNA polymerase II, with a strong evidence for bidirectional transcription according to the FANTOM5 CAGE database.
evidence: This is based on analysis of FANTOM5 CAGE data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The +3 kb region is conserved between mammals.
source: Finally, the region is conserved between mammals, pointing at its possible functional importance.
evidence: This is based on bioinformatic analysis of conservation shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The +3 kb region shows H3K27ac mark in the mouse forebrain, with the highest signal from embryonic day 14 to postnatal day 7.
source: We found that the +3 kb region shows H3K27ac mark in the mouse forebrain, with the highest signal from embryonic day 14 to postnatal day 7, but not in the heart or liver (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on analysis of H3K27ac ChIP-seq data from Nord et al., 2013 shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The +3 kb region does not show H3K27ac mark in the heart or liver.
source: We found that the +3 kb region shows H3K27ac mark in the mouse forebrain, with the highest signal from embryonic day 14 to postnatal day 7, but not in the heart or liver (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on analysis of H3K27ac ChIP-seq data from Nord et al., 2013 shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The +3 kb enhancer region might be active mainly in neural tissues in late prenatal and early postnatal life.
source: This suggests that the +3 kb enhancer region might be active mainly in neural tissues in late prenatal and early postnatal life.
evidence: This is an inference based on the H3K27ac ChIP-seq data analysis.

claim: The +3 kb region shows open chromatin structure in rat cortical and hippocampal neurons based on ATAC-seq analysis.
source: The ATAC-seq analysis was consistent with open chromatin structure of the +3 kb region, and the RNA-seq revealed possible eRNA transcription from the antisense strand (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on analysis of published ATAC-seq data from Carullo et al., 2020 shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: RNA-seq revealed possible eRNA transcription from the antisense strand of the +3 kb region in rat neurons.
source: The ATAC-seq analysis was consistent with open chromatin structure of the +3 kb region, and the RNA-seq revealed possible eRNA transcription from the antisense strand (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on analysis of published RNA-seq data from Carullo et al., 2020 shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The +3 kb region shows remarkable neuron specificity in human brain, as evident from open chromatin and H3K27ac histone mark, which are missing in microglia, oligodendrocytes, and astrocytes.
source: We found that the +3 kb region shows remarkable neuron specificity, as evident from open chromatin identified using ATAC-seq, and H3K27ac histone mark, which are missing in microglia, oligodendrocytes, and astrocytes.
evidence: This is based on analysis of human brain cell-type-specific ATAC-seq and ChIP-seq data from Nott et al., 2019 shown in Figure 1B.

claim: In humans, the +3 kb region shows the strongest eRNA expression in the brain, spinal cord, and olfactory region.
source: We found that in humans the +3 kb region shows the strongest eRNA expression in the brain, spinal cord, and olfactory region (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is based on analysis of FANTOM5 data using the Slidebase tool shown in Figure 1C.

claim: When grouped by cell type, the strongest expression of +3 kb eRNAs is in hair follicle cells, neurons, and trabecular meshwork cells.
source: When grouped by cell type, the strongest expression of +3 kb eRNAs is in hair follicle cells, neurons, and trabecular meshwork cells (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is based on analysis of FANTOM5 data using the Slidebase tool shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The +3 kb region is an evolutionarily conserved nervous system-specific enhancer that is active mostly in neural tissues and predominantly in neurons but not in other major brain cell types.
source: Collectively, this data suggests that the +3 kb region is an evolutionarily conserved nervous system-specific enhancer that is active mostly in neural tissues and predominantly in neurons but not in other major brain cell types.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on multiple lines of bioinformatic evidence presented in Figure 1 and supplements.

claim: In rat cultured cortical neurons, the +3 kb enhancer region showed very strong transcriptional activity (~300-fold higher compared to the promoterless luciferase reporter vector) that was independent of the orientation of the +3 kb region.
source: In rat cortical neurons, the +3 kb enhancer region showed very strong transcriptional activity (~300-fold higher compared to the promoterless luciferase reporter vector) that was independent of the orientation of the +3 kb region (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is based on luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The +11 kb negative control reporter showed very low luciferase activity in cortical neurons.
source: As expected, the +11 kb negative control reporter showed very low luciferase activity in cortical neurons.
evidence: This is based on luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The activity of the +3 kb region is upregulated ~2–3-fold in response to both KCl and BDNF treatment in neurons.
source: Our results indicate that the activity of the +3 kb region is upregulated ~2–3-fold in response to both stimuli, suggesting that the region could be a stimulus-dependent enhancer in neurons.
evidence: This is based on luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: In rat cultured cortical astrocytes, the +3 kb enhancer construct showed modest transcriptional activity (depending on the orientation ~6–23-fold higher compared to the promoterless vector control).
source: In rat cultured cortical astrocytes, the +3 kb enhancer construct showed modest transcriptional activity (depending on the orientation ~6–23-fold higher compared to the promoterless vector control, Figure 2C).
evidence: This is based on luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Dopamine treatment had no significant effect on the activity of the +3 kb construct in cultured cortical astrocytes.
source: However, dopamine treatment had no significant effect on the activity of the +3 kb construct in cultured cortical astrocytes, suggesting that this region is not a dopamine-activated enhancer in astrocytes.
evidence: This is based on luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The addition of the +3 kb enhancer region slightly increased the basal activity of Bdnf promoter I (~1.5–2-fold) in cultured cortical neurons.
source: For Bdnf promoter I (Figure 3B), the addition of the +3 kb enhancer region slightly increased the basal activity of the promoter region (~1.5–2-fold).
evidence: This is based on luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The +3 kb enhancer region potentiated the KCl- and BDNF-induced activity of Bdnf promoter I approximately threefold in an orientation-independent manner.
source: The +3 kb enhancer region also potentiated the KCl- and BDNF-induced activity of this promoter approximately threefold in an orientation-independent manner.
evidence: This is based on luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The addition of the +3 kb enhancer region potentiated the basal activity of Bdnf promoter IV approximately threefold.
source: Similar effects were observed for Bdnf promoter IV (Figure 3C), where the addition of the +3 kb enhancer region potentiated the basal activity of the promoter approximately threefold and KCl- and BDNF-induced activity levels approximately twofold.
evidence: This is based on luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The addition of the +3 kb enhancer region potentiated KCl- and BDNF-induced activity levels of Bdnf promoter IV approximately twofold.
source: Similar effects were observed for Bdnf promoter IV (Figure 3C), where the addition of the +3 kb enhancer region potentiated the basal activity of the promoter approximately threefold and KCl- and BDNF-induced activity levels approximately twofold.
evidence: This is based on luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The +11 kb intronic region failed to potentiate the activity of Bdnf promoters I and IV.
source: The +11 kb intronic region failed to potentiate the activity of Bdnf promoters I and IV.
evidence: This is based on luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figures 3B and 3C.

claim: The +3 kb enhancer failed to increase the activity of Bdnf promoters IV and VI in unstimulated astrocytes.
source: Notably, the +3 kb enhancer failed to increase the activity of Bdnf promoters IV and VI in unstimulated astrocytes and had little effect on the response of these promoters to dopamine (Figure 3D, E).
evidence: This is based on luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figures 3D and 3E.

claim: The +3 kb enhancer had little effect on the response of Bdnf promoters IV and VI to dopamine in astrocytes.
source: Notably, the +3 kb enhancer failed to increase the activity of Bdnf promoters IV and VI in unstimulated astrocytes and had little effect on the response of these promoters to dopamine (Figure 3D, E).
evidence: This is based on luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figures 3D and 3E.

claim: Targeting dCas9 without an effector domain to the +3 kb enhancer or +11 kb intronic region had no major effect on the expression of any of the Bdnf transcripts in cultured cortical neurons.
source: Targeting the +3 kb enhancer or +11 kb intronic region with dCas9 without an effector domain had no major effect on the expression of any of the Bdnf transcripts, indicating that targeting CRISPR complex to an intragenic region in Bdnf gene does not itself notably affect Bdnf gene expression (Figure 4, left panel).
evidence: This is based on RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4, left panel.

claim: Repressing the +3 kb enhancer region using CRISPRi decreased the basal expression levels of Bdnf exon I-, IIc-, and III-containing transcripts by 2.2-, 11-, and 2.4-fold, respectively, in cultured cortical neurons.
source: Repressing the +3 kb enhancer region using CRISPRi decreased the basal expression levels of Bdnf exon I-, IIc-, and III-containing transcripts by 2.2-, 11-, and 2.4-fold, respectively, although these effects were not statistically significant (Figure 4A–C, middle panel).
evidence: This is based on RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4A-C, middle panel.

claim: Repressing the +3 kb enhancer region using CRISPRi had no notable effect on basal levels of Bdnf exon IV-, VI-, and IXa-containing transcripts in cultured cortical neurons.
source: In contrast, no notable effect was seen for basal levels of Bdnf exon IV-, VI-, and IXa-containing transcripts (Figure 4D–F, middle panel).
evidence: This is based on RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4D-F, middle panel.

claim: Repressing the +3 kb enhancer region decreased the KCl and BDNF-induced levels of transcripts starting from the first three 5' exons ~4–7-fold in cultured cortical neurons.
source: Repressing the +3 kb enhancer region also decreased the KCl and BDNF-induced levels of transcripts starting from the first three 5' exons ~4–7-fold, but not of other Bdnf transcripts (Figure 4A–F, middle panel).
evidence: This is based on RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4A-F, middle panel.

claim: Targeting CRISPRi to the +11 kb intronic region had no notable effect on any of the Bdnf transcripts in cultured cortical neurons.
source: Targeting CRISPRi to the +11 kb intronic region had no notable effect on any of the Bdnf transcripts (Figure 4A–F, middle panel).
evidence: This is based on RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4A-F, middle panel.

claim: Activating the +3 kb enhancer region with CRISPRa in cultured cortical neurons increased the expression levels of Bdnf transcripts of the first cluster both in unstimulated neurons (~3–5-fold) and after KCl or BDNF treatment (~2-fold).
source: Activating the +3 kb enhancer region with CRISPRa in cultured cortical neurons increased the expression levels of Bdnf transcripts of the first cluster (Figure 4A–C, right panel) both in unstimulated neurons (~3–5-fold) and after KCl or BDNF treatment (~2-fold).
evidence: This is based on RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4A-C, right panel.

claim: Total Bdnf basal levels increased ~2-fold with CRISPR activation of the +3 kb enhancer region in cultured cortical neurons.
source: Total Bdnf basal levels also increased ~2-fold with CRISPR activation of the +3 kb enhancer region, whereas a slightly weaker effect was seen in stimulated neurons.
evidence: This is based on RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4G, right panel.

claim: Targeting CRISPRa to the +11 kb intronic region had no dramatic effect on the expression of any of the Bdnf transcripts in cultured cortical neurons.
source: As with CRISPRi, targeting CRISPRa to the +11 kb intronic region had no dramatic effect on the expression of any of the Bdnf transcripts, despite some minor changes reaching statistical significance (Figure 4A–F, right panel).
evidence: This is based on RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4A-F, right panel.

claim: Targeting CRISPRi to the +3 kb enhancer region in astrocytes did not decrease the basal expression levels of any Bdnf transcript.
source: Targeting CRISPRi to the +3 kb enhancer region in astrocytes did not decrease the basal expression levels of any Bdnf transcript (Figure 5, middle panel).
evidence: This is based on RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5, middle panel.

claim: In astrocytes treated with dopamine, repressing +3 kb enhancer region completely abolished the induction of exon IIc-containing transcripts.
source: In cells treated with dopamine, repressing +3 kb enhancer region completely abolished the induction of exon IIc-containing transcripts (Figure 5B, middle panel), but did not affect the expression of any other transcripts.
evidence: This is based on RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5B, middle panel.

claim: Activating the +3 kb region with CRISPRa greatly increased both basal and dopamine-induced levels of all measured Bdnf transcripts in astrocytes.
source: In contrast, activating the +3 kb region with CRISPRa greatly increased both basal and dopamine-induced levels of all measured Bdnf transcripts (Figure 5A–F, right panel).
evidence: This is based on RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5A-F, right panel.

claim: Targeting CRISPRi or CRISPRa to the +11 kb intronic control region did not have a noteworthy effect on any of the measured Bdnf transcripts in astrocytes.
source: Targeting CRISPRi or CRISPRa to the +11 kb intronic control region did not have a noteworthy effect on any of the measured Bdnf transcripts.
evidence: This is based on RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The +3 kb enhancer antisense eRNA was expressed in cultured neurons and the expression level of the eRNA was induced ~3.5- and ~6-fold upon BDNF and KCl treatment, respectively.
source: We found that the +3 kb enhancer antisense eRNA was expressed in cultured neurons and the expression level of the eRNA was induced ~3.5- and ~6-fold upon BDNF and KCl treatment, respectively.
evidence: This is based on RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Repressing the +3 kb enhancer region using CRISPRi decreased the expression of the eRNA ~3-fold.
source: Furthermore, repressing the +3 kb enhancer region using CRISPRi decreased the expression of the eRNA ~3-fold.
evidence: This is based on RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Activating the +3 kb enhancer region using CRISPRa did not change the expression level of the eRNA.
source: However, activating the +3 kb enhancer region using CRISPRa did not change the expression level of the eRNA.
evidence: This is based on RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Astrocytes showed ~6-fold lower eRNA transcription from the +3 kb enhancer region than neurons.
source: When comparing +3 kb enhancer eRNA expression levels in neurons and astrocytes, the astrocytes showed ~6-fold lower eRNA transcription from the +3 kb enhancer region than neurons (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), also indicating that the +3 kb region is in a more active state in our cultured neurons than in astrocytes.
evidence: This is based on RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The +3 kb enhancer region is an active enhancer of the Bdnf gene in rat cultured cortical neurons and regulates the basal and stimulus-induced expression of Bdnf transcripts of the first cluster of exons (exons I, II, and III).
source: Taken together, our results suggest that the +3 kb enhancer region is an active enhancer of the Bdnf gene in rat cultured cortical neurons and regulates the basal and stimulus-induced expression of Bdnf transcripts of the first cluster of exons (exons I, II, and III).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the CRISPRi and CRISPRa experiments shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: The +3 kb region is mostly inactive in rat cultured cortical astrocytes.
source: In contrast, the +3 kb region is mostly inactive in rat cultured cortical astrocytes.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the CRISPRi and CRISPRa experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: Deletion of the +3 kb enhancer region strongly decreased both the basal and stimulus-dependent expression levels of Bdnf exon I-, IIc-, and III-containing transcripts in mESC-derived neurons.
source: The deletion of the +3 kb enhancer region strongly decreased both the basal and stimulus-dependent expression levels of Bdnf exon I-, IIc-, and III-containing transcripts (Figure 7A–C).
evidence: This is based on RT-qPCR data from mESC-derived neurons shown in Figure 7A-C.

claim: The effect of +3 kb enhancer deletion was more prominent in clones containing homozygous deletion compared to heterozygous clones.
source: Notably, the effect was more prominent in clones containing homozygous deletion compared to heterozygous clones.
evidence: This is based on RT-qPCR data from mESC-derived neurons shown in Figure 7.

claim: The deletion of the +3 kb enhancer region decreased the total levels of Bdnf similarly to the first cluster of Bdnf transcripts in mESC-derived neurons.
source: The deletion of the +3 kb enhancer region decreased the total levels of Bdnf similarly to the first cluster of Bdnf transcripts (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is based on RT-qPCR data from mESC-derived neurons shown in Figure 7F.

claim: 21 transcription factors showed specific in vitro binding to the +3 kb enhancer region compared to the +11 kb intronic region in two independent experiments.
source: Collectively, we determined 21 transcription factors that showed specific in vitro binding to the +3 kb enhancer region compared to the +11 kb intronic region in two independent experiments (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is based on in vitro DNA pulldown assay coupled with mass spectrometry shown in Figure 8B.

claim: Numerous E-box-binding proteins, including USFs, TCF4 and the pro-neural transcription factors NeuroD2 and NeuroD6, bind to the +3 kb enhancer region.
source: Of note, we found numerous E-box-binding proteins, including USFs, TCF4 and the pro-neural transcription factors NeuroD2 and NeuroD6, possibly providing the neuron-specific activity of the +3 kb enhancer region.
evidence: This is based on in vitro DNA pulldown assay coupled with mass spectrometry shown in Figure 8B.

claim: JunD, a member of the AP-1 transcription factor family, binds to the +3 kb enhancer region.
source: We also detected binding of JunD, a member of the AP-1 transcription factor family.
evidence: This is based on in vitro DNA pulldown assay coupled with mass spectrometry shown in Figure 8B.

claim: CREB binds to the +3 kb enhancer region in cultured cortical neurons.
source: We performed ChIP-qPCR and determined that in cultured cortical neurons CREB binds to the +3 kb enhancer region, whereas we found no significant CREB binding to the +21 kb negative control region, located directly downstream of Bdnf exon VII (Figure 8D).
evidence: This is based on ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 8D.

claim: The binding of CREB to the +3 kb enhancer region was ~2.6 times stronger than binding to Bdnf promoter IV.
source: Of note, the binding of CREB to the +3 kb enhancer region was ~2.6 times stronger than binding to Bdnf promoter IV, which contains the well-described CRE element (Hong et al., 2008; Tao et al., 1998).
evidence: This is based on ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 8D.

claim: TCF4 binds to the +3 kb region in cultured neurons.
source: As transcription factors from the NeuroD family need dimerization partner from the class I helix–loop–helix proteins, for example, TCF4, to bind DNA (Massari and Murre, 2000; Ravanpay and Olson, 2008), we verified the binding of TCF4 to the +3 kb region in our cultured neurons using TCF4 ChIP-qPCR (Figure 8D).
evidence: This is based on ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 8D.

claim: Dominant negative versions of CREB (A-CREB), ATF2 (A-ATF2), and AP-1 family (A-FOS) showed the strongest inhibitory effect on +3 kb enhancer activity in luciferase reporter assays.
source: In agreement with the in vitro pulldown assay, ChIP-seq and ChIP-qPCR results, we found the strongest inhibitory effect using dominant negative versions of CREB (named A-CREB), ATF2 (named A-ATF2), and AP-1 family (named A-FOS).
evidence: This is based on luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 8E.

claim: Silencing TCF4 expression with TCF4 shRNA decreased the activity of the +3 kb enhancer region in both unstimulated and KCl- and BDNF-stimulated neurons.
source: Using luciferase reporter assays, we found that silencing TCF4 expression with TCF4 shRNA-expressing plasmid decreased the activity of the +3 kb enhancer region in both unstimulated and KCl- and BDNF-stimulated neurons.
evidence: This is based on luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 8F.

claim: A putative E-box binding sequence (CAGATG) exists in the +3 kb enhancer region.
source: Based on the TCF4 and NeuroD2 ChIP-seq data (Figure 8C), we identified a putative E-box binding sequence in the +3 kb enhancer region (CAGATG).
evidence: This is based on analysis of ChIP-seq data and sequence analysis.

claim: The E-box motif (CAGATG) participates in regulating both the basal activity and BDNF- and KCl-induced activity of the enhancer region.
source: We determined that this motif participates in regulating both the basal activity and BDNF- and KCl-induced activity of the enhancer region (Figure 8G).
evidence: This is based on luciferase reporter assay data with E-box mutations shown in Figure 8G.

claim: Mutating the E-box decreased the ability of the +3 kb enhancer region to potentiate transcription from Bdnf promoter I in reporter assays.
source: Importantly, mutating the E-box decreased the ability of the +3 kb enhancer region to potentiate transcription from Bdnf promoter I in reporter assays (Figure 8H).
evidence: This is based on luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 8H.

claim: Bdnf promoters I, II, and III are located within a relatively compact (~2 kb) region in the genome.
source: Bdnf promoters I, II, and III are located within a relatively compact (~2 kb) region in the genome, making it possible that their activity is controlled by a common mechanism.
evidence: This is based on knowledge of the Bdnf gene structure.

claim: Spatial clustering of Bdnf exons seems to be conserved in vertebrates.
source: Spatial clustering of Bdnf exons seems to be conserved in vertebrates (Keifer, 2021), with a similar genomic organization observed in frog (Kidane et al., 2009), chicken (Yu et al., 2009), zebrafish (Heinrich and Pagtakhan, 2004), rodents (Aid et al., 2007), and human (Pruunsild et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Bdnf exon I-containing transcripts contain in-frame alternative translation start codon that is used more efficiently for translation initiation than the canonical start codon in exon IX.
source: We have previously reported that exon I-containing Bdnf transcripts contain in-frame alternative translation start codon that is used more efficiently for translation initiation than the canonical start codon in exon IX (Koppel et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research from the authors' laboratory.

claim: In female mice, Bdnf exon I-containing transcripts are important for proper sexual and maternal behavior.
source: In female mice, Bdnf exon I-containing transcripts are important for proper sexual and maternal behavior (Maynard et al., 2018), whereas in male mice the Bdnf exon I- and exon II-containing transcripts regulate serotonin signaling and control aggressive behavior (Maynard et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: In male mice, Bdnf exon I- and exon II-containing transcripts regulate serotonin signaling and control aggressive behavior.
source: In female mice, Bdnf exon I-containing transcripts are important for proper sexual and maternal behavior (Maynard et al., 2018), whereas in male mice the Bdnf exon I- and exon II-containing transcripts regulate serotonin signaling and control aggressive behavior (Maynard et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Bdnf exon I-containing transcripts in the hypothalamus participate in energy metabolism and thermoregulation.
source: Furthermore, it has been shown that Bdnf exon I-containing transcripts in the hypothalamus participate in energy metabolism and thermoregulation (You et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The highest H3K27ac modification at the +3 kb enhancer region in development occurs a week before and a week after birth in mice.
source: The data from Nord et al., 2013 indicates that the highest H3K27ac modification, a hallmark of active regulatory region, at the +3 kb enhancer region in development occurs a week before and a week after birth in mice – coinciding with the period of late neurogenesis, neuronal migration, synaptogenesis, and maturation of neurons (Reemst et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on analysis of published ChIP-seq data from Nord et al., 2013.

claim: The +3 kb enhancer region is mostly active in early life and participates in the development of the central nervous system via regulating Bdnf expression.
source: It appears that the +3 kb enhancer region is mostly active in early life and participates in the development of the central nervous system via regulating Bdnf expression.
evidence: This is an inference based on the developmental expression pattern of H3K27ac at the +3 kb region.

claim: The part of the Bdnf gene containing the +3 kb enhancer has previously been implicated in the Reelin-mediated induction of Bdnf expression.
source: Notably, the part of the Bdnf gene containing the +3 kb enhancer has previously been implicated in the Reelin-mediated induction of Bdnf expression (Telese et al., 2015), indicating that the +3 kb enhancer could respond to other stimuli in addition to membrane depolarization and TrkB signaling.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Other distal enhancer regions form chromatin loops with the Bdnf first cluster of exons and the +3 kb enhancer region.
source: Recently, it has been shown that other distal enhancer regions form chromatin loops with the Bdnf first cluster of exons and the +3 kb enhancer region (Beagan et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Long-distance interactions with the +3 kb enhancer region have been reported in neurons isolated from the human brain.
source: Similarly, long-distance interactions with the +3 kb enhancer region have been reported in neurons isolated from the human brain (Nott et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: CTCF and RAD21 bind near the +3 kb enhancer region.
source: Furthermore, CTCF and RAD21, both important regulators of the chromatin 3D structure (Rowley and Corces, 2018), seem to bind near the +3 kb enhancer region (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on analysis of ENCODE ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: The +3 kb enhancer could partially mediate its effect on Bdnf gene expression by regulating the higher-order chromatin structure in the Bdnf gene locus.
source: Therefore, it is possible that the +3 kb enhancer could partially mediate its effect on Bdnf gene expression by regulating the higher-order chromatin structure in the Bdnf gene locus by bringing together distal enhancer regions and Bdnf promoters from the first cluster of exons.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about a possible mechanism.

claim: The +3 kb region is not the enhancer responsible for catecholamine-dependent induction of Bdnf expression in astrocytes.
source: Furthermore, the transcriptional activity of the +3 kb enhancer was not induced by dopamine treatment in luciferase reporter assay, further indicating that the +3 kb region is not the enhancer responsible for catecholamine-dependent induction of Bdnf expression.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on luciferase reporter assay data in astrocytes.

claim: The +3 kb enhancer region might control the activity of stimulus-specific expression of Bdnf promoter II in astrocytes.
source: Interestingly, the dopamine-dependent induction of Bdnf exon IIc-containing transcripts was abolished when the +3 kb enhancer was repressed using CRISPRi, suggesting that the +3 kb enhancer region might control the activity of stimulus-specific expression of Bdnf promoter II in astrocytes.
evidence: This is an inference based on CRISPRi data in astrocytes.

claim: The +3 kb enhancer is a positive regulator of Bdnf gene operating specifically in neurons.
source: Although we have not tested it directly, our data does not support the notion that the +3 kb region is an active repressor in non-neuronal cells, for example, astrocytes. Instead, it seems that the +3 kb enhancer is a positive regulator of Bdnf gene operating specifically in neurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the overall experimental data.

claim: The +3 kb enhancer region is distinct from the distal cis-regulatory region controlling the catecholamine-induced activities of Bdnf promoters IV and VI in astrocytes.
source: We conclude that the +3 kb enhancer region is largely inactive in rat cultured cortical astrocytes and it is distinct from the distal cis-regulatory region controlling the catecholamine-induced activities of Bdnf promoters IV and VI.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data in astrocytes.

claim: mRNAs of NeuroD transcription factors are expressed mainly in excitatory neurons, similar to Bdnf.
source: Single-cell RNA-seq analysis in the mouse cortex and hippocampus has indicated that mRNAs of NeuroD transcription factors are expressed mainly in excitatory neurons, similar to Bdnf (Tasic et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: NeuroD2 preferentially binds to E-boxes CAGCTG or CAGATG.
source: It has been reported that NeuroD2 preferentially binds to E-boxes CAGCTG or CAGATG (Fong et al., 2012), which is in agreement with the functional E-box CAGATG sequence found in the +3 kb enhancer.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: NeuroD2 knock-out animals exhibit decreased Bdnf mRNA and protein levels in the cerebellum.
source: Furthermore, it has been previously shown that NeuroD2 knock-out animals exhibit decreased Bdnf mRNA and protein levels in the cerebellum (Olson et al., 2001).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: NeuroD transcription factors regulate neuronal differentiation.
source: It has been well described that NeuroD transcription factors regulate neuronal differentiation (Massari and Murre, 2000), axonogenesis (Bormuth et al., 2013), neuronal migration (Guzelsoy et al., 2019), and proper synapse formation (Ince-Dunn et al., 2006; Wilke et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: At least some of the effects carried out by NeuroD family may result from increasing Bdnf expression.
source: As BDNF also has a role in the aforementioned processes (Park and Poo, 2013), it is plausible that at least some of the effects carried out by NeuroD family result from increasing Bdnf expression.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the known functions of both NeuroD and BDNF.
